dedupe_keys.name: mosaik co simulation platform coupling opendss a refined ns 3 network simulator and python controllers for smart grids

description: This preprint presents a co-simulation platform based on the Mosaik framework that links OpenDSS power flow, a refined NS-3 communication-network simulator and custom Python simulators for on-load tap changer control, distributed state estimation and data collection. It compares exhaustive lock-step time advancement with an event-driven scheme that uses lower-bound time stamps and next-event prediction, adds refinements to NS-3 event handling, and reports up to 50 percent shorter execution time (more than four times in smaller cases) on the IEEE 13-node feeder and a 33-bus system with 32 European low-voltage feeders (1,793 nodes). A domain ontology for multi-simulator configuration is summarised. Producer: University of Alberta researchers; submitted to arXiv on 2 September 2026 (15 pages). Coverage: benchmark power systems with a communication layer. Access: paper on arXiv; no code repository is linked on the abstract page, so no open-source release is verified. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: only the abstract page was read here and results are on standard benchmarks. Simulation uses: it couples telecom network behaviour to power distribution studies of cyberattacks and extreme events. Related records: none linked.
